newsitem.title: USA: Florida citrus belt stays dry, some growth showing.
newsitem.headline: Florida citrus belt stays dry, some growth showing.

text.p: Virtually all areas of the Florida citrus belt were dry again for the week ended Nov 11, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS) said, with some young tree groves in the southern and coastal regions still showing some young growth.
There were a few passing showers on Friday, followed by cool and pleasant temperatures during the weekend, FASS said.
Harvest is increasing for both fresh and processed utilization and more than half the state's processing plants are open, Fass said.

According to FASS, caretakers are mowing and chopping cover crops for fire control prior to harvesting, and some cover crops that have grown out of control are causing various problems with low volume irrigation water distribution.
Additionally, FASS estimated 258,000 boxes of Navel oranges were harvested in the week ended November 11, up from 211,000 boxes in the previous week and 198,000 boxes in the week ended October 27.
An estimated 2,037,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended November 11, up from 547,000 boxes the prior week and 290,000 boxes the week ended October 27, FASS said.
